title: Audit logging: model metadata change events + changelog publish actions (SIEM field mapping)
author: Kevin Osei
release_notes: Internal: emits audit events for model metadata updates and changelog publish actions; adds SIEM export mapping and validation tests.
body:
Title: Audit logging: model metadata change events + changelog publish actions (SIEM field mapping)

Context
We’re standardizing model/version metadata and generating customer-visible model changelog entries from registry change-events. Enterprise/security reviews (e.g., SUP-18421 / FinchBank-style questionnaires) require immutable, attributable audit logs for (a) metadata edits and (b) release-note publication actions. This PR adds first-class audit log entries for those actions and defines a stable SIEM export mapping so Security/GRC can answer “who changed what, when, from where, and what was published”.

Scope
1) Emit audit events for model metadata create/update/deprecate operations
2) Emit audit events for changelog workflow actions (draft->in_review->published, publish, rollback/supersede)
3) Add a canonical field mapping for SIEM export (Datadog + Splunk HEC)
4) Add tests + fixtures to ensure we never leak internal-only metadata in audit payloads

Non-goals
- This does not implement retention/immutability storage guarantees end-to-end (that’s handled by audit store configuration + WORM settings in the audit sink); it does add the fields needed to support those guarantees.
- This does not change customer-facing changelog content or template logic.

Implementation details

Audit event types
We now emit the following audit event types from the control plane:
- redwood.model_metadata.create
- redwood.model_metadata.update
- redwood.model_metadata.deprecate
- redwood.changelog_entry.create_draft
- redwood.changelog_entry.transition_state (captures draft->in_review->published and rejects)
- redwood.changelog_entry.publish
- redwood.changelog_entry.supersede (used by rollback/correction; preserves history)

Event envelope
All events share a common envelope to make SIEM queries consistent:
- audit.event_id (UUIDv7)
- audit.event_time (RFC3339)
- audit.event_type
- audit.environment (prod|staging|dev)
- audit.actor.user_id
- audit.actor.email
- audit.actor.role (rbac role name)
- audit.actor.ip
- audit.actor.user_agent
- audit.request.request_id
- audit.request.route
- audit.request.method
- audit.request.org_id (tenant)

Resource fields (for model metadata)
- target.model_id
- target.version_id
- target.deployment_modes (hosted|dedicated|private)
- target.visibility (internal|customer_visible)
- target.change_summary (string, redacted; see below)
- target.changed_fields (comma-separated list of field paths; internal-only list, safe for audit)

Resource fields (for changelog publish)
- target.changelog_entry_id
- target.model_id
- target.version_id
- target.previous_state
- target.new_state
- target.publication_target (docs|console_api|feed)
- target.published_url (when available; empty for drafts)
- target.supersedes_entry_id (for corrections)

Redaction / “don’t leak internal metadata”
Audit logs must be attributable and useful but must not become an internal-data exfil channel. This PR enforces:
- For model metadata updates, we do NOT record raw before/after JSON blobs.
- We include changed field names (paths) and a short, human-readable change_summary generated from an allowlisted set of field paths.
- Any values coming from fields marked internal-only are replaced with “[REDACTED]” in change_summary.
- We explicitly exclude: vendor contract identifiers, internal model nicknames, unreleased eval links, and capacity/region routing policies.

SIEM export mapping
We export to a flattened schema for both Datadog logs and Splunk HEC. Below is the mapping (left: Redwood event JSON, right: SIEM field).

Common
- audit.event_id -> event.id
- audit.event_time -> @timestamp
- audit.event_type -> event.action
- audit.environment -> labels.env
- audit.request.request_id -> trace.id
- audit.request.route -> http.request.path
- audit.request.method -> http.request.method
- audit.actor.ip -> network.client.ip
- audit.actor.user_agent -> user_agent.original
- audit.actor.user_id -> user.id
- audit.actor.email -> user.email
- audit.actor.role -> user.roles
- audit.request.org_id -> organization.id

Targets
- target.model_id -> redwood.model.id
- target.version_id -> redwood.model.version
- target.changelog_entry_id -> redwood.changelog.entry_id
- target.published_url -> url.full
- target.publication_target -> redwood.changelog.publish_target
- target.changed_fields -> redwood.audit.changed_fields
- target.change_summary -> message

Notes
- We intentionally put a redacted human summary in message to support on-call triage without requiring deep JSON inspection.
- changed_fields remains available for precise filtering (e.g., “who changed deprecation.sunset_date?”).

Files / areas changed (high level)
- control-plane/audit/events.go: new event constructors and shared envelope
- control-plane/model-registry/handlers/*.go: emit audit events on create/update/deprecate
- control-plane/changelog/workflow/*.go: emit audit events on transitions/publish/supersede
- security/audit/sinks/{datadog,splunk}.go: export mapping + field normalization
- security/audit/redaction/*.go: allowlist + redaction utilities
- test/audit/*: golden fixtures verifying field mapping + redaction

Example events (sanitized)
1) Metadata update
- event_type: redwood.model_metadata.update
- target.model_id: rwd-llama-3-70b
- target.version_id: 2026-02-18
- changed_fields: provenance.source, compatibility.tool_calling, limits.context_window
- change_summary: “Updated provenance source and compatibility notes; context window clarified.”

2) Publish
- event_type: redwood.changelog_entry.publish
- target.changelog_entry_id: clg_01JKT2...
- published_url: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/model-release-notes/rwd-llama-3-70b/2026-02-18
- publication_target: docs

Testing
- Unit tests: redaction allowlist, mapping normalization, event envelope required fields
- Integration-ish tests: simulate a metadata update + publish action; verify two audit events emitted with expected SIEM fields

Operational considerations
- Volume: metadata edits and publish actions are low volume; safe to emit synchronously with request handling. We still gate export retries to avoid request tail latency.
- Failure mode: if SIEM sink is down, we enqueue to audit buffer (existing component) and return success unless buffer is full; in that case we fail closed for publish actions (publish must be auditable) and fail open for non-customer-visible metadata edits (configurable; default open for now).

Checklist
- [x] Adds audit event types for metadata + changelog publish
- [x] Includes actor + request context
- [x] Redacts internal-only fields
- [x] Adds SIEM mapping docs in-code + tests
- [x] Validated in staging with Splunk HEC

Screenshots / Logs
- Attached in internal staging run: see CI artifact “audit-fixtures-18821” (golden outputs)

Review conversation

Marcus Lin (Security)
> We need to ensure publish actions “fail closed” if we can’t write an audit event. Otherwise we can’t assert completeness for enterprise change-management.

Kevin Osei (Author)
Good call. I changed behavior so changelog_entry.publish and supersede fail closed if audit buffer enqueue fails. Metadata updates remain fail-open by default (configurable), consistent with existing audit guidelines. Added test coverage for the fail-closed path.

Olga Petrov (GRC)
> Can we include a stable “organization id” and “actor role” field for audit questionnaires? Also clarify retention isn’t handled here.

Kevin Osei
Added audit.request.org_id and audit.actor.role into the common envelope and mapped them into SIEM fields (organization.id, user.roles). Added a comment block in sinks to explicitly state retention/WORM configuration is out of scope for this PR.

Jordan Lee (Policy/RBAC)
> For transition_state events, include previous_state and new_state and make sure it’s emitted on reject as well.

Kevin Osei
Done: transition_state now always includes previous_state/new_state and is emitted for approve/reject transitions. Added fixtures for both approve and reject.

Jada Williams (Workflow)
> Any risk that change_summary includes internal evaluation names?

Kevin Osei
We do not include eval URLs or eval suite names in change_summary; those fields are not in the allowlist. I added an explicit deny rule for eval.* paths to avoid future regressions.

CI
- build (linux_amd64): pass
- unit_tests: pass
- lint: pass
- security_scan: pass
- integration_tests (staging harness): pass

Merge
- Squash merged into main

Follow-ups
- ENG-4930: add dashboards/alerts for audit sink lag/failures
- PM-803: document emergency publish path + audit expectations for operators (link to runbook)
